source.locations: Svendsen et al. (2023), Structural Health Monitoring 22(1):540-561, Figure 3(b) (schematic of damage locations), read at 400 dpi
source.sensor_coordinates: data/derived/hbta/edge_spectra_multicondition_10s.npz (origin at midspan; x east, y north)

reading_conventions: Figure 3(b) is an oblique view with west on the left and the south lower chord at the front, as in Figure 3(a).
Floor beams are at x = -17.5, -14, ..., 17.5 m (10 panels of 3.5 m); AL sensors are at panel midpoints.
Stringer cross beams are drawn at panel midpoints, between the two stringers.
Positions read from the schematic are uncertain by about one panel; the alternatives below cover this.
rule: A damage state is represented by weakening all springs whose structural path passes through the damaged connection or member, using the relation type that represents that member type.

folders_checked_without_new_location_inf: E:/09 VERY BIG DATA/05_Bridge_Hell_Railway_Truss/DOCS (landing pages, drawings as scans; h5 attributes have state labels but no locations)
decision_stringer_rows: Each stringer is represented by its inner-row path (y = -0.55 south, +0.55 north), as in the submitted DS1 analysis, so that the DS1 results reported to the reviewers are unchanged. The outer-row path (y = -0.95 / +0.95) of the same stringer is reported as a sensitivity case for DS1 and DS2.

evaluation_plan.link_level: Spearman between q of the damaged spring set and measured link response R, per state; bootstrap CI; compared with graph-distance and Euclidean-distance baselines. DS5 and DS6 reported but flagged as not detectable.
evaluation_plan.location_agnostic_restoration: Lower-tail restoration choices compared with baselines on measured TPR averaged over, and minimum across, the detectable states (DS1-DS4, DS7, DS8), using the stored single- and pair-outage detector results; larger outages re-run with the same detector and threshold.
evaluation_plan.sensitivity: Every alternative set listed above is evaluated and reported, whatever the outcome.
